repository.note: NE not applicable by design (200 = exists)

blocking.issue: A failed PR association (pulls not 200, e.g. a curl-mode 403 rate limit, 404, 422 or 000; or the lowest PR's GET failing so base_ref is empty) is treated as 'no associated PR'. reviews, timeline, protection, branch_rules and rulesets are then labelled NOT_EVIDENCED_ON_HOST, so a 403/404 is mislabelled as absence.
blocking.fix: Take the no-PR branch only when pulls is 200 and the list is empty, and the no-base branch only when pulls/{n} is 200 and base_ref is empty. Otherwise label NOT_ACCESSIBLE with the upstream status in note.

blocking.issue: Channels that were never called get NOT_EVIDENCED_ON_HOST, which contradicts the protocol's own rule 'not called -> NOT_ACCESSIBLE'. rulesets is repository-scoped and needs no base branch, so skipping it and asserting absence is a negative by construction. Having no PR does not show that the commit's branch is unprotected.
blocking.fix: Always call rulesets. When there is no base, label protection and branch_rules NOT_ACCESSIBLE ('not called: no base derivable'). Limit the special case in the protocol to reviews and timeline after a 200 with an empty list.

blocking.issue: Derived kv and prs.tsv fields are written whatever the HTTP status, defaulting to false or 0. ch_protection.tsv on the expected curl-mode 401/403/404 reports required_pull_request_reviews/enforce_admins/required_status_checks/required_signatures/push_restrictions/allow_force_pushes=false. A failed pulls/{n} gives merged=false and n_reviews=0. These files carry no http column.
blocking.fix: Write derived values only when the source status is 200. Otherwise write http=<status> and NOT_DETERMINABLE for every derived field.

nonblocking.issue: No observation time is recorded (neither the host Date header nor the client clock), so current-state channels are unanchored in time. Add both, labelled, to summary.json.
per_page=5 returns the host's first 5 PRs before sorting, so 'lowest numbers first' is not guaranteed. cap_reached flags the possibility.
WHY is always 'call budget reached' (L181), so a transport failure on ev1 (000, L161) gets the wrong note. The existence value is still correct.
checks, runs, rulesets and branch_rules have no *_truncated flags. The checks HOST_GENERATED decision covers only the returned page. status is called without per_page.

The note on L113 contains 'GitHub Actions'. If a raw git user object has the name 'GitHub' (web-flow committer), the whole-word guard fails and the run exits 5 with no output. This fails safe but can waste a run.
Timeline events without created_at (e.g. line-commented) are counted as outside the window but labelled created_at=HOST_GENERATED.

If git is absent, the 'any git work tree' refusal is silently skipped. mkdir -p after the existence check is a TOCTOU gap (use mkdir). grep -I can skip NUL-containing files. Stage writes other than summary.json are unchecked.
Role logins are passed as jq --arg, so they are visible in /proc/*/cmdline, and jq stderr errors can quote raw values. Neither reaches OUT.
repo_slug_sha256 is an unsalted hash of a known slug: an integrity tag, not anonymisation.
In curl mode a 200 [] for rulesets can come from hidden entries. It is covered by the declared coverage loss, but the rulesets row note should state it.
